title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Global Supply Chains and Sustainable Production
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Parts for a coffee maker are made in Country K and sold for $24 (assume the parts maker buys no inputs). A factory in Country M assembles the coffee maker and sells it to a store for $41. The store sells it for $72. How many dollars of value does the assembly stage add? (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: A firm buys a key part from a single low-cost supplier. It is considering adding a second supplier that charges a higher price. What is the main trade-off?

choices.text: It raises costs in normal times but lowers the risk of a production stop
It lowers costs in normal times but raises the risk of a production stop
It raises costs in normal times and also raises the risk of a production stop
It leaves normal costs unchanged but makes production more exposed to disruption

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A dyeing plant in Country S pollutes a river, harming people downstream. The finished shirts are sold in Country D, and the plant pays nothing for the damage. Which statement best describes the shirts' price in Country D?

choices.text: It equals the shirts' social cost, because buyers in Country D are not harmed
It is above the shirts' social cost, because transport costs are included
It equals the private cost, so the external cost disappears after export
It is below the shirts' social cost, because the external cost is left out

questions.prompt: Which SDG target most directly encourages large and transnational companies to adopt sustainable practices and include sustainability information in their reporting?

Hypothetical example: A firm faces a 20% chance each year of a supply disruption that would cost it $150,000. A backup supplier contract costs $25,000 a year and would cut that loss to $50,000. Comparing expected yearly costs, which statement is correct?

choices.text: The backup contract lowers expected yearly cost by $5,000
The backup contract lowers expected yearly cost by $75,000
The backup contract raises expected yearly cost by $5,000
The backup contract raises expected yearly cost by $25,000
